Class ChartSvgSanitizer

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.report.pdf.ChartSvgSanitizer
public final class ChartSvgSanitizer extends Object
Admits only the kind of SVG that Plotly draws for a chart and refuses everything else. The SVG arrives from the browser and Batik, which renders it for the PDF, would otherwise follow references to files and web addresses, and run scripts. Nothing is repaired: a document with an element or attribute outside the list is rejected as a whole, because a chart that silently lost parts would be printed as if it were complete.

The checks are: a parser without document type declarations and external entities, a fixed list of SVG elements, no event handler attributes, no href at all, references in url(...) only to an id inside the document, and size limits. The one change made to an accepted document is the font: every font-family is replaced by the bundled font, because the PDF can only embed that one.
